name: G479, one rule everywhere: a transfer its source cannot fund is excluded on BOTH legs (Harbour has 100 and is due to send 300, Meadow has 50 and pays 120): one shortfall, one cover move, total 30

expected.notes: Today is Thu 19 Nov 2026, pay is the last Friday, so payday is Fri 27 Nov: the window is 19 to 26 Nov. Harbour Current holds 100 and has a standing order of 300 to Meadow Current on Mon 23 Nov (day 4). Meadow Current holds 50 and pays home insurance 120 on Tue 24 Nov (day 5). No income is expected. G479 (Kevin 2026-11-19, "all figures must be consistent"): a transfer between counted current accounts whose source cannot fund it (the G360 test: the source's cash after the order and its other payments that day is 100 - 300 = -200, below zero) is excluded on BOTH legs on every surface: Meadow is not credited the 300 and Harbour is not debited it. Harbour keeps its 100 with no dip (after payments 100, low point 100, covered). Meadow: 50 - 120 = -70 on 24 Nov, short by 70 (after payments -70, low point -70). Left to spend: 100 + (-70) = 30, which is the pooled 100 + 50 - 120. Exactly one shortfall (Meadow 70) and one cover move: the shortfall 70 is already a multiple of 5, plus the 10 cushion = 80, taken from Harbour (headroom 100 - 10 = 90, enough alone). Harbour sets 80 aside (100 - 80 = 20), Meadow's dip is covered by the move in (-70 + 80 = 10, requires the move); 20 + 10 = 30, the dip counted once. The line names it: 'Meadow Current: £70 short on 24 Nov' (no money follows it). At risk count 1: the insurance. The ledger, Upcoming, the cover plan, the at-risk badge and the client walk all read the same events (before this rule the ledger credited Meadow 300 while the gated walks did not, so Meadow showed no dip on Home and 70 short on Upcoming).
